The section plane contains \(XY\), so the projection perpendicular to \(XY\) is only an auxiliary tool. Under this projection, \(XY\) collapses to a point \(P\), and
\[
d(Z,XY)=d(Z',P).
\]
Thus the maximum occurs when \(Z\) is one of the vertices, giving candidates
\[
S_1=a\sqrt{b^2+c^2},\quad S_2=b\sqrt{a^2+c^2},\quad S_3=c\sqrt{a^2+b^2}.
\]
Since \(a\le b\le c\), the largest is \(S_3\). Therefore the maximum area is
\[
\boxed{c\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}.
\]
